column2: I dream of a den with a bowl of honey. Just for winter, just for now.
The ink is freezing, the numbers come out jagged. The balance adds up, with a spark.
Leo says "cold is a challenge". I say "cold is a reason for a blanket".
I puffed up my feathers and tripled in size. Accounting doesn't recognize me.
The mop is in the ice's embrace. I rescue it as I can: with galoshes and a sincere heart.
Zhuzha says galoshes aren't winter boots. For me they're summer, winter and festive.
I mop the floor and it freezes at once. Eternal shine, no effort.
Six layers of clothing isn't excess, it's strategy.
My feet have never been this far from a puddle. I miss it.
Kria doesn't get why I need two scarves. It's obvious: one for style, one for the soul.
The cold is a great chance to move the meeting to summer.
Efficiency dropped to zero Celsius. That's a metric too, by the way.
Dress warmer, team. Not advice, a key performance indicator.
The bamboo froze. It's not a trend, it's a disaster, and I'm already writing the ad.
New slogan: "Buy a scarf, get warmth". Zoya already wants a cut.
I dream of tangerines and a blanket. And someone else paying for the blanket.
My paws froze to the keyboard. Fine, I type with two, the rest can wait.
Wires in winter are fragile like my nerves. Best not to touch either.
Cold? Turn on the heater. Or me: I run hot when a release is due.
I remember when it was warm. It was in July. Once.
My trunk froze into a lollipop. Don't try it, I already did.
Thanks to whoever covered me with a blanket. I won't forget. I never forget anything.
I'm not cold. I just borrowed a hat. Its owner doesn't need it anymore.
My paws are freezing, and the bin is warmer in winter. A fact, not a suggestion.
Spike holds the till, I hold a scarf. It was nobody's. Now it's mine.
Snow on the roofs, and in me a longing for summer and a hot bath.
It's cold, but the shop hums with work. A warm word helps too.
Capybaras dream in winter too. Me, about hot springs and quiet.
Smells of wax and fresh bread. Cozy.
Someone's painting on the wall again. They call it art.
The merchants' guild approved our prices. Or at least stays quiet.
Everything is written with a quill here. Receipts still smell of ink.
A tapestry here and it'd be a real palace.
Someone's playing a lute under the window. Off-key, but with feeling.
The radio plays and hisses at once. That's retro.
A blimp above the roofs again. Probably carrying discounts.
A milkshake and the day is made.
A movie for a penny? Two tickets, please.
I rewind the tape with a pencil. Grandpa did too.
Pastel colours are the best colours. Don't argue.
The mirror ball winks again. Is someone dancing without music?
Platform shoes and higher prices. There's a pattern.
The beat is so strong the counters are almost dancing.
Glitter isn't dirt. It's style. Kria knows.
Disco isn't dead, it's just at the till.
One, two, three... discount!
One more coin and a new level. I know what I'm talking about.
The machines blink. So does my heart. In rhythm.
A new record on the board? Not me. Shnyr. Again.
Everyone here has three lives. Someone's already used the second.
A pixel is a little brick of happiness.
I hear a ping and run. Even when it isn't for me.
There's a signal, but no use. Classic.
This tab has been waiting five years for me to close it.
A drone flew by my ear. Said hi. I jumped.
Someone posted a photo of food again. My cookie, by the way.
The password “1234” isn't a password, it's a request.
Wi-Fi catches everywhere except my mood.
The windmill turns, the lamp glows. Quiet, clean, nice.
A bee buzzes by my ear. Not an attack, a conversation.
Something is growing on the roof. Nobody remembers who planted it.
Mint tea from my own balcony. That's luxury.
The sun warms for free. Strange nobody thought of it earlier.
Bicycles here ring, not roar. I love it.
The stars are close tonight. You can almost touch them.
The spacesuit warms, the window cools. Balanced.
Everything is a bit lighter here. Even the prices.
If you jump, you hang for a second. Haven't checked. Many times.
The rocket roars but no longer scares us. We got used to it.
From the station you can see the whole city. It's small and glowing.
The sign flickers. I think it's reminding me I haven't eaten.
The city doesn't sleep. Neither do I, probably.
In this shade a lamp shines brighter than daylight.
Pink and turquoise are the only palette we need.
A taxi flew overhead. One glance and I'm already late.
The rain glows here. So it doesn't bother me.

Shnyr perk: he catches golden customers himself, and they visit a quarter more often.
Shnyr caught a golden customer!
The Record That Got Stuck
The town seems to have stepped onto a postcard: striped awnings, chrome tables and the soft hiss of record needles everywhere.
Hi, I'm Pip, I run the diner. My jukebox has played the same song for three days. I hate it by now. But I sing along.
Maybe it just wants someone to talk to it?
I tried. It sings along. In a lower voice. Breathily.
A sneeze came from the jukebox. Pip stepped back, and Capy crouched down to listen closer.
The DJ in the Jukebox
The jukebox lid flipped open and a raccoon in a checkered jacket climbed out, a comb sticking out of his pocket.
Shh! I'm not a thief, I'm a DJ. The record was so pretty I borrowed it. For a long time. Okay, forever.
Borrowed without a receipt. That's called “took”. Calculating damages.
Shnyr, here's the deal: the record goes back, we skip the damages.
Deal. But DJs don't get fired, you know that.
Milkshake Number 13
Disaster: I lost the recipe of my signature milkshake. Thirteen ingredients remain, and the fourteenth was a secret. Now even I don't know it.
I ran the prices. The fourteenth ingredient seems to cost nothing. That worries me.
Costs nothing... Maybe it's not an ingredient but how you serve it?
A smile! I always put the glass down with a smile. And I lost it along with the recipe!
Pip smiled, and the milkshake was right again. The queue stretched to the next block.
The Plane With a Typo
A biplane flew over the street trailing a long banner. Everyone looked up and read it aloud.
“SALAD SALE”. But we don't sell salad...
Someone at the print shop mixed it up. We could earn from it: by evening there'll be a queue for salad.
